title: The Delhi Sultanate
subtitle: Five dynasties that ruled from Delhi · 1206 – 1526
subject: delhi-sultanate
intro: For 320 years a succession of Turkic and Afghan dynasties ruled north India from Delhi — the Mamluks, Khaljis, Tughlaqs, Sayyids and Lodis. They held off the Mongols, carried their armies to the far south under Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughlaq, and built the Qutb Minar and the early cities of Delhi. Overstretch, revolts and Timur's sack of Delhi in 1398 broke their power, and Babur ended the Sultanate at Panipat in 1526.

members.name: Short reigns
members.note: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq II, Abu Bakr Shah, Muhammad Shah III, Ala ud-din Sikandar Shah

members.name: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah

events.title: Iltutmish defeats Yildiz
events.summary: At Tarain Iltutmish defeats Taj al-Din Yildiz, a rival heir of Muhammad of Ghor, and secures his throne.

events.title: Razia overthrown and killed
events.summary: The Turkish nobles depose Razia; she is killed near Kaithal after a failed attempt to recover the throne.

events.title: Nasiruddin Mahmud — Balban as regent
events.summary: A pious young sultan takes the throne while his deputy Balban runs the state for twenty years.

events.title: Balban dies
events.summary: Balban's death leaves the throne to his pleasure-loving grandson Qaiqabad; the Khaljis seize power three years later.

events.title: Alauddin murders his uncle
events.summary: Returning rich from Devagiri, Alauddin has Jalaluddin killed at Kara and marches on Delhi, buying support with Deccan gold.

events.title: Mongols crushed at Amroha
events.summary: Alauddin's generals destroy a Mongol army at Amroha; the Mongol threat to Delhi recedes.

events.title: Malik Kafur reaches Madurai
events.summary: After sacking the Hoysala capital, Malik Kafur raids as far as Madurai in the Pandya country.

events.title: Alauddin dies
events.summary: Alauddin dies; Malik Kafur briefly rules through a child sultan before he too is murdered.

events.title: Tughlaqabad built
events.summary: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq builds the fortress city of Tughlaqabad, legend says cursed by the Sufi saint Nizamuddin.

events.title: Ghiyasuddin killed
events.summary: A wooden pavilion built to welcome him collapses on the sultan at Afghanpur; his son Muhammad becomes sultan.

events.title: The Deccan breaks away
events.summary: Revolting nobles in the Deccan found the Bahmani Sultanate at Gulbarga.

events.title: Firuz Shah dies
events.summary: Firuz Shah dies at an advanced age; succession struggles weaken the Tughlaqs on the eve of Timur's invasion.

events.title: Jaunpur breaks away
events.summary: The governor of the east founds the Sharqi Sultanate of Jaunpur.

events.title: Sikandar Lodi succeeds
events.summary: Bahlul Lodi dies; his son Sikandar strengthens the sultanate and later moves the court to Agra.

events.title: Ibrahim Lodi succeeds
events.summary: Ibrahim Lodi's attempts to curb the Afghan nobles turn many of them against him.

events.title: Defeat by Rana Sanga
events.summary: Rana Sanga of Mewar defeats Ibrahim Lodi's army, showing how weak the sultanate has become.

events.title: Daulat Khan invites Babur
events.summary: Daulat Khan Lodi, governor of the Punjab, invites Babur to help overthrow Ibrahim — an invitation Babur turns into conquest.

events.title: Second Battle of Tarain
events.summary: Muhammad of Ghor defeats Prithviraj Chauhan, a year after losing to him on the same field. The Ghurids take Delhi and Ajmer, and Muhammad leaves his slave-general Qutb ud-Din Aibak in charge of his Indian conquests.

events.title: Qutb Minar begun
events.summary: Aibak begins the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, built partly from the material of demolished temples, and the Qutb Minar beside it. Iltutmish completes the tower's upper storeys.

events.title: Aibak becomes Sultan
events.summary: After Muhammad of Ghor is assassinated, Aibak rules his Indian territories independently from Lahore — the start of the Delhi Sultanate and of the 'Mamluk' or Slave dynasty, named for its founders' origins as military slaves.

events.title: Aibak dies; Iltutmish takes the throne
events.summary: Aibak dies after a fall from his horse while playing polo at Lahore. His son-in-law Iltutmish, governor of Badaun, sets aside Aibak's son Aram Shah and makes Delhi the capital.

events.title: The Mongols at the Indus
events.summary: Genghis Khan defeats Jalal al-Din Mangburni at the Indus. Iltutmish declines to shelter the fugitive prince, and the Mongols turn back — the first of many Mongol threats to the Sultanate.

events.title: Recognised by the Caliph
events.summary: Iltutmish receives a robe of investiture from the Abbasid caliph in Baghdad, confirming him as sovereign Sultan. He organises revenue grants (iqta) to his officers and a coinage of silver tankas.

events.title: Razia Sultan
events.summary: Iltutmish names his daughter Razia as his heir. After her brother's brief reign she rules for four years, appearing in public in a man's dress, before nobles depose and kill her in 1240.

events.title: Balban's iron rule
events.summary: Balban, long the power behind the throne, becomes Sultan. He breaks the power of the Turkish nobles, insists on elaborate court ceremony and the Sultan's divine authority, and fortifies the north-west against the Mongols.

events.title: The Khalji revolution
events.summary: Jalaluddin Khalji overthrows the last Mamluk sultans, opening the Sultanate's ruling class to non-Turkish nobles.

events.title: Alauddin's raid on Devagiri
events.summary: Alauddin, Jalaluddin's nephew, makes a surprise raid on the Yadava capital of Devagiri. With its treasure he murders his uncle and takes the throne.

events.title: Battle of Kili
events.summary: A large Chagatai Mongol army reaches the outskirts of Delhi; Alauddin's army forces it to withdraw. Further invasions in 1303 and 1305 are also repelled.

events.title: Ranthambore taken
events.summary: After a long siege Alauddin takes Ranthambore from Hammir Dev Chauhan.

events.title: Siege of Chittorgarh
events.summary: Alauddin captures Chittor from Ratnasimha. The later poem Padmavat (1540) built the famous legend of Rani Padmini around this siege; contemporary chronicles do not mention her.

events.title: Alauddin's market and revenue reforms
events.summary: To pay a huge standing army against the Mongols, Alauddin fixes prices in Delhi's markets, raises land revenue to half the produce, and builds the new city of Siri.

events.title: Malik Kafur's southern campaigns
events.summary: Alauddin's general Malik Kafur leads armies against Devagiri (1308), the Kakatiyas at Warangal (1310), the Hoysalas (1311) and Madurai (1311), returning with vast plunder and tribute.

events.title: Alai Darwaza
events.summary: Alauddin adds the Alai Darwaza, a domed gateway with true arches and red-sandstone and marble decoration, to the Qutb complex.

events.title: Amir Khusrau and Nizamuddin Auliya
events.summary: The poet and musician Amir Khusrau, who served several sultans, and his master, the Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya, make Delhi a centre of Persian and Hindavi poetry and Sufi devotion.

events.title: The Tughlaqs take power
events.summary: Ghazi Malik, the frontier governor, overthrows the usurper Khusrau Khan and becomes Sultan as Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq. He builds the fortress-city of Tughlaqabad.

events.title: Kakatiya kingdom annexed
events.summary: Prince Ulugh Khan, the future Muhammad bin Tughlaq, takes Warangal and annexes the Kakatiya kingdom.

events.title: Muhammad bin Tughlaq
events.summary: Muhammad bin Tughlaq comes to the throne — learned, ambitious and erratic. Under him the Sultanate reaches its greatest extent.

events.title: The capital moved to Daulatabad
events.summary: Muhammad orders Delhi's elite and much of its population to move to Devagiri, renamed Daulatabad, to govern the Deccan. The experiment is abandoned within a few years.

events.title: Token currency
events.summary: Muhammad issues copper and brass coins with the value of silver. Mass forgery forces him to withdraw them and redeem the tokens from the treasury.

events.title: Ibn Battuta in Delhi
events.summary: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta arrives in Delhi and serves Muhammad as a judge for several years; his account is a vivid source on the court.

events.title: Provinces break away
events.summary: Revolts follow one another: the Madurai Sultanate (1335), the Vijayanagara kingdom (1336), Bengal and the Bahmani Sultanate of the Deccan (1347) all become independent.

events.title: Firuz Shah Tughlaq
events.summary: Firuz Shah gives up further conquests and concentrates on administration: canals, new towns, and the palace-city of Firozabad (Feroz Shah Kotla). He also extends the jizya to Brahmins.

events.title: An Ashokan pillar moved to Delhi
events.summary: Firuz Shah has an Ashokan pillar brought from Topra in the Punjab and erected at Firozabad — its Brahmi inscription unreadable to anyone at the time.

events.title: Hauz Khas madrasa
events.summary: Firuz Shah builds a madrasa and his own tomb beside Alauddin's reservoir at Hauz Khas.

events.title: Timur sacks Delhi
events.summary: Timur defeats the Tughlaq army outside Delhi and sacks the city for days, killing much of its population. The Sultanate never recovers its former power; regional sultanates in Jaunpur, Gujarat and Malwa rise.

events.title: The Sayyid dynasty
events.summary: Khizr Khan, who had served Timur as governor of Multan, takes Delhi. The Sayyids rule a shrunken kingdom for under forty years.

events.title: The Lodis
events.summary: Bahlul Lodi, an Afghan noble from the Punjab, takes power and conquers the Jaunpur Sultanate, partly restoring the Sultanate in the north.

events.title: Sikandar Lodi founds Agra
events.summary: Sikandar Lodi founds a new capital at Agra, later the Mughals' first capital.

events.title: Lodi tombs
events.summary: The Sayyid and Lodi sultans are buried in domed tombs in what are now Delhi's Lodi Gardens.

events.title: First Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Babur, invited by disaffected Lodi nobles, defeats and kills Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat. The Delhi Sultanate ends and the Mughal Empire begins.
